0.long_answer: Bloom syndrome is a rare autosomal recessive genetic disorder caused by mutations in the BLM gene, which encodes a RecQ DNA helicase. This mutation leads to chromosomal instability, characterized by an increased rate of sister chromatid exchanges and a high predisposition to various types of cancer. Affected individuals typically exhibit short stature, a sun-sensitive skin rash, and an increased risk of developmental abnormalities. The syndrome was first described by Dr. David Bloom in 1954 and remains a key example of how defects in DNA repair mechanisms can result in significant clinical consequences.
